full_judgment:
94. In judicial review of administrative actions, the Court has to start with the presumption of regularity of the official act and the burden of proof is on the person who alleges the contrary. Whenever a power is given by statute to an authority, whatever may be fairly regarded as incidental to or consequential upon things authorized by legislature should not be declared ultra vires (AG vs Great Eastern Rly Co (1880) 5 APP case 473). The Courts should not compel a public authority by issuing a writ of mandamus to perform an act which are within its domain. In Islamic Republic of Pakistan vs Muhammad Sneed, 13 DLR (SC) 94, Hamoodur Rahman, J argued after considering English and American decisions on the principle of the powers of the High Court to issue direction or order for any purpose to any person or authority including any Government in respect of writ of mandamus as under: 

 125. Admittedly, the writ-respondent-appellants did not file any affidavit-in-opposition in any of the writ petitions either controverting the case of the writ-petitioners as made out in the writ petitions or stating their own version on the claim of the writ-petitioners. In view of the above, we have tried to see the case of the writ-respondent-appellants from the civil petition for leave to appeal as well as from the concise statement filed before this Division, but we did not find any case of the writ-respondents. Although in the leave granting order, it appears that the learned Additional Attorney-General while making submissions referred to page-39 of the additional paper book filed in Leave Petition No. 1275 of 2005 (CA Appeal No. 127 of 2005) to point out that the Director of Sea Fisheries Department, Agrabad, Chittagong in his communication dated 22-9-2003 made it clear that the trawler was allowed to fish for two weeks at a time subject to various conditions and there was no stipulation that the trawler would be permitted to fish at its free will and that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that since Pakistan period, the exclusive economic territory for Marine Fisheries was utilised and after liberation some individual brought technology from abroad and the Government declared Marine sector as an industry, but the resources of the country being limited as per joint venture survey report made by Russia and Japan, the Government adopted some policies with regard to culturing, hatching (in the leave granting order it has wrongly been written as hedgering) and catching fishes within 200 nautical miles; that the High Court Division failed to consider that at a subsequent stage, a high powered technical committee of experts named as "Zaman Committee" was formed and its survey report was found to be in harmony with the survey report of the donors stating that without further survey number of trawlers except the existing 73 should not be increased, otherwise, it would create adverse effect on the Marine resources of the country and that the Government decided to increase the licences of fishing trawlers by another 40 for granting licences in 4 categories inviting by advertisement through paper on fulfillment of certain requirements, but the petitioners did not comply with such requirements, i.e. the body of the trawler must be steel body and the applicant must have bank solvency certificate to show that he/it was capable of spending taka 5 (five) crore for each trawler, but these facts have not been stated either in the leave petition or in the concise statement. To be precise, we are constrained to say that in the leave petition as well as in the concise statement, no fact whatsoever, on behalf of the writ-respondent-appellants has been stated. Therefore, the case of the writ-petitioner-respondents as stated in the writ petitions, particularly the fact that the trawlers of the petitioners are fishing trawlers which were seized by the Government of Bangladesh while they were fishing illegally within the Bangladesh territorial waters and subsequently those were sold in auction conducted by the concerned Government functionaries and were purchased by the petitioners with the expectation that those will be used for deep sea fishing and after purchase, the petitioners made necessary repair works and made all of them ready and fit for being used as fishing trawlers in the deep sea by spending huge amount of money and a technical committee formed by the authority to enquire as to the fitness of the trawlers of some of the petitioners found them fit for deep sea fishing and in other cases, fitness certificates were issued by the Mercantile Marine Department and Naval Architecture and Marine Engineer after due inspection of the trawlers and also, on their application, temporary fishing licences were given to some of them for fishing in the deep sea remained uncontroverted before the High Court Division as well as before this Division. It is true that the writ- petitioners have to succeed of their own, even the writ-respondents do not controvert their case, but when in the writ petitions, a positive case of 'legitimate expectation' was asserted and in support of the case, documents were annexed thereto, in the absence of any denial of the assertions of the writ-petitioner's case as well as the annexure annexed to the petitions, their case cannot altogether be rejected or ignored. In this regard, it is necessary to state that as regards the pleading of the parties in a writ petition, the principles of Order VI of the Code of the Civil Procedure will be applicable both in respect of writ petition as well as the affidavit-in-opposition; while in case of suits, the plaint and the written statement should contain only facts and not evidence, in the writ petition and in the affidavit-in-opposition not only facts, but also the evidence in proof of the facts stated therein need be pleaded and annexed. Facts stated in the writ petition are to be controverted by filing an affidavit-in-opposition and if any statement made in the writ petition is not controverted in the affidavit-in-opposition, the Court is to proceed as if such statements have been admitted by the respondent(s), similarly if facts asserted in the affidavit-in-opposition are not controverted by filing an affidavit-in-reply shall be deemed to have been admitted and therefore, the writ-respondents were required to state necessary facts in denial of the case of the writ-petitioners by filing affidavit-in-opposition before the High Court Division and at least in the concise statement. We like to observe further that the writ-respondents be it the Government and the other Government functionaries or a private individual cannot be allowed to argue or make submissions on fact unless they plead such fact by filing affidavit-in-opposition or in the concise statement.
